title: Enforce a token-bucket limit
statement:
Step 4 · Caching and admission

A token bucket permits bursts up to capacity and refills over time. Rejected requests do not consume tokens. A distributed limiter needs an atomic state update and a clock policy.

Build it

Start with a full bucket at time 0. For each [time_seconds,cost], refill to at most capacity, then accept only if enough tokens remain. Events are ordered with nondecreasing nonnegative times; capacity and costs are positive, refill is nonnegative.

Contract: Implement allow using Python's standard library. Inputs satisfy the constraints stated here. Do not mutate the inputs. Use the provided helpers where present; they represent earlier steps.

Examples

Input: capacity = 3, refill_per_second = 1, events = [[0, 2], [0, 2], [1, 2], [1, 1], [5, 3]]
Expected: [true, false, true, false, true]
Input: capacity = 1, refill_per_second = 0, events = [[0, 1], [10, 1]]
Expected: [true, false]
Hint

Advance the refill timestamp for every event, including rejected requests.

Review your understanding

How would concurrent workers share this bucket? What should happen when the backing store is unavailable?

Explain your reasoning in Notes before opening the worked solution. Passing the local checks completes this exercise; it does not certify production readiness or evaluate your design explanation.

references.python:
class Solution:
    def allow(self, capacity: float, refill_per_second: float, events: list[list[float]]) -> list[bool]:
        tokens=capacity
        last=0.0
        accepted=[]
        for now,cost in events:
            tokens=min(capacity,tokens+(now-last)*refill_per_second)
            ok=tokens>=cost
            if ok:tokens-=cost
            accepted.append(ok)
            last=now
        return accepted
